key_insight: SOMA provides a unified body layer that bridges diverse parametric human models (SMPL, SMPL‑X, MHR, Anny, etc.) via three abstraction layers, enabling loss-minimized interoperability across mesh topology, skeletons, shape spaces, and unit conventions.
problem_solved: Parametric human body models are mutually incompatible in mesh topology, skeletal structure, shape parameterization, and units, which prevents combining their complementary strengths in a single reconstruction/animation/simulation pipeline.
method: Define a canonical representation and three abstraction layers (topology, skeletal/joint mapping, and shape/pose/units) that mediate between model-specific formats.
Implement bidirectional mappings/converters that preserve geometry and semantics to translate models to/from the SOMA canonical layer with minimal loss.
Expose a modular API/layer that integrates into existing reconstruction, animation, and simulation pipelines to enable mixed-model workflows and dataset reuse.
impact: Makes it practical for AI/ML practitioners to mix and match parametric body models and datasets, improving flexibility, interoperability, and overall performance in 3D human reconstruction, animation, and simulation workflows.
visual_elements: Central hub diagram: multiple models (SMPL, SMPL‑X, MHR, Anny) with arrows mapping to/from a SOMA canonical model

paper_title: SOMA: Unifying Parametric Human Body Models
paper_authors: Jun Saito, Jiefeng Li, Michael de Ruyter, Miguel Guerrero, Edy Lim
